authors: Takeshi Sako, Toshikatsu Hakuta, Hiroshi Yoshitome
title: Vapor Pressures of Binary (H2O-HCl, -MgCl2, and -CaCl2) and Ternary (H2O-MgCl2-CaCl2) Aqueous Solutions
needs_pass2_reason: Text layer was clean for all tables (two-column layout scrambled a few lines in text order only); every cell was compared against the 200 dpi page images; no cell needed correction.
experimental_method: All-glass Bourdon gauge (glass spiral with pointer read by cathetometer, nitrogen back-pressure measured with a mercury manometer); solution degassed under vacuum; 320-400 K; sample molality analysed after the run (EDTA titration for Mg and Ca, density at 293.2 K for HCl).
uncertainties_stated: Precision of measurement +-0.1 K or +-70 Pa, whichever is larger (abstract); gauge sensitivity 40 Pa; composition analysis within 0.3 %; pure-water check: max deviation 213 Pa, mean 67 Pa.
quality_remarks: Paper states the discrepancy of MgCl2 osmotic coefficients with literature (especially at 1 mol/kg). Ternary solution measured vapor pressures are 0.6-3.6 kPa above both the authors' Antoine-type calc and Teruya-method values, mean dev 2.00 kPa. Temperature scale not stated. The PDF starts with the last page (224) of another article (end of an excess-enthalpy paper, glossary/references) which precedes the Sako title on the same page, and its last page (228) holds only the Sako references and the start of another article; neither contributes data.
not_extracted_tables: Table I (HCl aqueous solutions, p. 225): HCl is outside the in-scope salt set, no in-scope component other than water.
Table IV (parameters of the Antoine-type equation): model parameters, fitted.
Figures 2-5 (log p vs 1/T, boiling points of HCl, osmotic coefficients of MgCl2 and CaCl2 vs T): derived/plotted, no tables.

row_counts.table_2: printed 30 data rows, written 30 (+4 label rows, +4 mean-dev rows)

extraction_notes: p(calcd) and dev columns are the authors' fit (Antoine-type) and are kept in the CSV, unmapped. Label rows give the molality of each block ('x mol/kg'); the printed 'mean dev' rows are kept as summary rows and listed in skip_rows. Table V has a constant composition (1.057 mol/kg MgCl2 and 2.905 mol/kg CaCl2) given in its title, mapped as composition.constant. Sanity: p rises monotonically with T in every block; highest p about 160-163 kPa; at equal T, p decreases with molality in Tables II and III. Table II data lie in 322.6-397.8 K, Table III 322.7-402.7 K, Table V 322.5-398.2 K. The paper has no calibrated T scale and no pressure basis other than vapor pressure of the solution.
pass2_diff: Tables 2, 3, 5: every pass-1 number occurs in pass 2; the extra pass-2 numbers are the printed mean-dev rows and the Table 5 label, which pass 1 skipped.
